findings.title: The step output 'carry_exit' is captured but never consumed; refusal enforcement relies solely on the payload file. Behavior is still fail-closed (missing/!ok payload publishes failure and fails the job), so this is dead code, not a hole.
findings.body: The step output 'carry_exit' is captured but never consumed; refusal enforcement relies solely on the payload file. Behavior is still fail-closed (missing/!ok payload publishes failure and fails the job), so this is dead code, not a hole. Evidence: echo "carry_exit=$?" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" is written; the subsequent 'Publish PR Steward status' step reads only $RUNNER_TEMP/carry.json and never references steps.carry.outputs.carry_exit. Location: .github/workflows/merge-queue-carry-forward.yml (Carry forward step)

findings.title: status_state reads a single page of the combined-status endpoint with no pagination, unlike check_conclusion which paginates. Worst case is a false refusal (fail-closed) if the context's latest status falls beyond the first page; it cannot produce a false carry because statuses are returned newest-first.
findings.body: status_state reads a single page of the combined-status endpoint with no pagination, unlike check_conclusion which paginates. Worst case is a false refusal (fail-closed) if the context's latest status falls beyond the first page; it cannot produce a false carry because statuses are returned newest-first. Evidence: payload = self._api(f"commits/{sha}/status") with no per_page/page loop; first matching context is returned. Location: scripts/ci/merge_queue_carry_forward.py, GhApi.status_state

findings.title: Check-run collection stops after 10 pages (1000 runs). If API ordering were not newest-first and >1000 same-name runs existed on one sha, the true highest-id run could be missed and an older success treated as newest. Theoretical only; also the API default filter=latest already returns the newest run per name/app.

findings.title: TOCTOU window: gates on immutable PR-head shas are evaluated at carry time; a rerun completing with failure on the same sha after the queue job succeeded would not retroactively revoke the already-published queue-commit success. Window is small and requires an unusual same-sha rerun.
findings.body: TOCTOU window: gates on immutable PR-head shas are evaluated at carry time; a rerun completing with failure on the same sha after the queue job succeeded would not retroactively revoke the already-published queue-commit success. Window is small and requires an unusual same-sha rerun. Evidence: The workflow publishes state on merge_group.head_sha once; nothing re-validates the PR-head gates between job completion and the queue's merge. Location: scripts/ci/merge_queue_carry_forward.py, evaluate / workflow timing

remaining_risks: Enforcement depends on branch protection / merge-queue rules (outside this diff) actually requiring the 'independent embedded audit' check and 'PR Steward / final readiness' status on queue commits; the workflow only publishes them.

Gate authenticity depends on only trusted apps/workflows being able to create check runs named 'independent embedded audit' or statuses named 'PR Steward / final readiness' on PR heads; name-based trust is inherited from the existing Grok/AGY producers, not established here.

If GitHub changes the gh-readonly-queue ref format, parse_queue_pr_numbers returns None and the name-vs-parent refusal check is skipped (all parents are still individually gated, so this degrades safely).
